added_failures_source.derived_by: reckon/crew/review.py added_failures_from_gate_logs over the text of the 51 + 50 logs the manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite log_path values name
added_failures_source.note: those log_path values are directories, so annotate_review_of_run records this count as unmeasured at read time; the count and ids above are the derivation from the logs those directories hold

findings.text: the baseline_suite and after_suite log_path values on this line and line 21 name a directory rather than a log, so reckon/crew/review.py:645 _read_gate_log returns None for both and every review of this run is annotated added_failure_count: null with "names no base gate log" (reproduced: logs/added-failure-derivation.log in the reviewing run) although the 201 logs under those directories are readable and yield count 1; the total cap of 5 is therefore skipped now and would bite the moment the path is repaired, because the only prose naming of the id is the failure_attribution mapping at manifest.md:22 and the token _retires_id (reckon/crew/review.py:717) builds from it carries the commit suffix and matches no id.

the two suite observations do not satisfy the repository's own completeness validator: reckon.ledger.suite_observation_missing_fields reports baseline_suite.exit_status and after_suite.exit_status (exit_status is the prose string "mixed: 44 of 51 exit 0, 7 exit 1" where an int is required) and after_suite.failure_count_matches_failure_ids (4 failing runs against 1 distinct id); crew check-manifest stays green because it does not apply that validator, and this run was not armed so nothing refused it, but the shape is what an armed run's evidence is validated against.

"only reckon/cli.py differs" is not true of the trees the arms ran: 327 tracked paths differ between 16423b79 and 4f37ffe8 (38 under reckon/, 56 under tests/, 229 under docs/); the sentence's load-bearing half (the test file's md5 is identical across all four trees, which I verified) is what makes the arms comparable, so the localisation clause overstates and invites reading any rate difference as cli.py-only.

"which the time fence did not allow" is not supported by the run's own record: it exited at 16:37:14Z, 31.9 minutes into its 50-minute fence, having spent 14.5 minutes of pytest across all 201 runs (mean 4.33 s), so the two 50-run arms this follow-on names cost about 7 minutes of the 18 that remained, and the stated reason misdescribes that cost to whoever picks the work up.
